Subject: Data residency follow-ups from today

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo this morning. Great overview. A few follow-up items that came up internally as we validate options for our procurement/SecOps review:

1) Region pinning: can you confirm whether we can pin traffic and all customer data to a single EU region (e.g., eu-west-1) and prevent automatic cross-region failover unless we opt in?
2) Backups & DR: where are backups stored by default? Are snapshots/replicas ever stored in a non-EU region? What is the restore SLA from backups?
3) PII & logs: can you confirm that PII (names, identifiers) is not used for analytics outside the region? Where are request logs and audit logs stored, and who has access?
4) KMS / key management: do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for data at rest in the EU deployment?

We're trying to capture clear yes/no/notes for each so we can pass to procurement and InfoSec. If you can provide a short written summary plus any artifacts (SOC2 / DPA) that would help.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Miller
Senior IT Risk Manager, Acme Bank

Hi Sara,

Really appreciate the clear list. Below is a concise summary; Aditya and Sean (copied) will add technical and compliance details. I've attached a simple region-pin architecture diagram and our SOC2 summary per your ask.

Quick answers:
- Region pinning: YES - per-tenant region pinning to a chosen EU region (eu-west-1) is supported. Automatic cross-region failover is opt-in and controlled by your config (we do not enable cross-region replication by default).
- Backups & DR: Backups are stored encrypted in the pinned region by default. Cross-region replication is optional and requires explicit opt-in. Restore SLA depends on plan - standard: 24-72 hours; expedited restore (Dedicated/Private) available via paid runbooks.
- PII & logs: PII is stored in-region. Application request logs and audit logs can be kept in-region; platform telemetry (aggregated, non-PII) may be routed to our control plane for monitoring unless you choose a Private deployment. Role-based access controls govern log access.
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via major KMS providers in the region.

Next steps I propose:
1) Aditya to share a short technical note (region pinning + backup replication behavior + sample config).
2) Sean to share the SOC2 summary and DPA/DPA addendum path and confirm audit log options.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to confirm procurement requirements and final config.

I've put a 30-min tentative on Wed Apr 1 10:00 CET - feel free to propose an alternate.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: Data residency follow-ups from today - technical details

Hi Sara,

Following up with technical specifics for the items you flagged. TL;DR: we can meet all of the EU residency requirements you described with configuration choices; details below.

1) Region pinning
- Per-tenant region pinning is implemented at the routing layer and storage layer. When enabled, all runtime instances, KV caches, and object stores for that tenant are provisioned in the selected region.
- Failover: cross-region failover is off by default. If you opt in, we replicate encrypted snapshots to the DR region; failover is an explicit action (automated runbooks can be enabled).

2) Backups & DR
- Default behavior: encrypted snapshots are stored in the pinned region (S3-equivalent in eu-west-1).
- Cross-region replication: available as an opt-in configuration; replicated snapshots remain encrypted with your CMK if BYOK is used.
- Restore SLA: standard restore ~24-72 hours (depends on dataset size); for Reserved/Dedicated customers we provide expedited restore runbooks (target <8 hours for typical DB sizes).

3) PII & logs
- PII handling: we treat PII as customer data; it is stored and processed in-region by default.
- Logs: two classes - audit logs (request-level, user-access events) and telemetry (anonymized metrics). Audit logs can be configured to stay in-region and to be shipped to your storage endpoint (S3 bucket) in the same region. We also support disabling platform-level telemetry export if required.
- Access: RBAC + IAM roles; we maintain strict access controls and can provide a list of roles with access to logs.

4) KMS / BYOK
- We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and GCP KMS. Keys can be region-scoped and used for all at-rest encryption and snapshot encryption.

Attached: redwood-region-pinning-diagram.pdf (architecture), sample config snippet for tenant pinning.

If it helps, I can produce a short runbook describing steps to enable region pinning + optional replication and the implications for cost and RTO.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer - Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-region-pinning-diagram.pdf

Hi Sara,

Confirmations in short bullets for procurement packet:
- Audit logs: YES - retention configurable; we can set tenant audit-log retention to 90 days and export logs to your eu-west-1 S3 bucket via a customer-supplied bucket policy.
- Backups: YES - by default backups/snapshots are stored in the pinned region (eu-west-1). Cross-region replication is off by default and requires explicit opt-in; restores occur in-region unless replication is enabled.
- BYOK: YES - snapshots and at-rest storage can be encrypted with your AWS KMS CMK (eu-west-1). We support key policies and use envelope encryption so your key never leaves the region.

- redwood-region-pinning-diagram.pdf (architecture)

- redwood-data-retention-policy.pdf (retention defaults and how to customize)
